post.contentHtml:
A Malaysian Infrastructure Group Listed on the Tokyo Exchange

YTL Corporation (Tokyo code 1773) is a Malaysian infrastructure conglomerate that operates construction, hotels, cement, real estate, and power, water and telecommunications businesses in Malaysia. Its closing price on the provided reference date (2026-11-13) was ¥77, and its one-year price change was -15.38%. We could not confirm the closing price for 2026-11-20, so the share price figures below are as of November 13.

The Theme of This Article: The Stock Is Weak, but Earnings Are Shifting Toward Data Centers

What stands out is the gap between the Tokyo share price and the momentum of the core business. According to Malaysian local media, YTL Group's fourth-quarter results for fiscal 2026 (year ended June 2026) improved significantly from the previous quarter.

Item (April–June 2026 quarter)Details
RevenueAbout 8.82 billion ringgit, up 16% from the previous quarter
Net profit after taxAbout 750 million ringgit, up 19% from the previous quarter
Profit before taxAbout 1.19 billion ringgit, up 38% from the previous quarter

In contrast, in the preceding third quarter (January–March), net profit fell compared with the same period a year earlier. Results fluctuated from quarter to quarter and rebounded in the fourth quarter. The company also announced that it increased its annual dividend.

Why Data Centers Are the Key

  • According to reports, the data center business's pre-tax profit grew more than tenfold, from about 32 million ringgit a year earlier to about 350 million ringgit.
  • Revenue is rising as "data halls" (server room units within a data center) come online in stages.
  • The company plans to expand its green data center park in Kulai, Johor, Malaysia from 600MW to 1,000MW, and has also announced the joint development of a gigawatt-class campus in the Sedenak area. (MW is a unit of power capacity and a yardstick for data center scale.)

Because data centers need a great deal of electricity, YTL, which owns power generation operations, may benefit from linking power and data centers. However, this is an interpretation of its business structure, and actual profitability depends on customer contracts and utilization rates.

Ownership Structure: A Stable Controlling Shareholder

  • Founding family holding company (Yeoh Tiong Lay & Sons Holdings): 47.29%
  • Malaysia's public pension fund (EPF): 12.44%
  • PNB (state-backed investment institution): 2.49%

Compared with the end of September, the changes in holdings were at the second decimal place, so there was effectively no major change. With the owner family and domestic institutions holding more than half, the governance is stable, but it also means the free float may be relatively small. The Korean National Pension Service is confirmed not to hold the stock.

Risks Investors Must Check

  • Low trading volume: The median annual trading value on the Tokyo market is only about ¥699,000. It may be hard to buy or sell at the price you want.
  • Currency risk: The business is conducted in Malaysian ringgit while the shares trade in yen, so exchange rate effects compound.
  • Earnings volatility: There have been cases where quarterly results swung widely depending on electricity tariff levels and the cement and construction cycle.
  • Heavy investment burden: Expanding data centers requires enormous capital, and delays in bringing capacity online could become a burden.

Summary

YTL is a case of a traditional infrastructure company growing a new pillar of growth in data centers. That effect showed up in this quarter's results, but the Tokyo-listed shares trade very thinly and have declined over the past year. The key point to watch is whether data center growth continues in the first-quarter results of the new fiscal year (reportedly due in late November, though the schedule should be confirmed in company disclosures).

This article is not investment advice, and responsibility for investment decisions rests with the investor.
